agentUtterance.text: In order to fix the issue, we will run our Virtual Repair process. Some tests take several minutes to run and while troubleshooting, your services may be temporarily disrupted. This process is also available through the MyBell app and has written instructions with images specific to the equipment in your home. Also, we noticed you are calling from a home phone. Your call will likely get disconnected as we're restarting services connected to your landline. To prevent the call from disconnecting, we recommend to either hangup and call us from a mobile phone or by using the Virtual Repair tool through the MyBell App. Before I start the process, did you want me to send the link to the device you're calling from to run Virtual Repair in the MyBell app instead?
Ok, let me get a live agent on the line to help you with this.

playbookInput.precedingConversationSummary: user asks bot for help so they can resume the services

playbookOutput.executionSummary:
This interaction shows a customer needing internet troubleshooting, initially declining the self-serve Virtual Repair tool via an app, and eventually agreeing to a guided process over the phone.
The conversation begins with the customer stating their internet isn't working. The agent responds by suggesting the Virtual Repair tool through the My Bell app, explaining its diagnostic capabilities and efficiency in streamlining support. The agent also offers to send a text with instructions.

The customer declines this offer. The agent then explains the necessity of Virtual Repair as a foundational troubleshooting step, emphasizing that it performs the same tests as live representatives. They reiterate the benefits of the app, such as visual instructions, and offer the alternative of conducting the process over the phone if the app isn't preferred.

The customer again declines the app-based option. Acknowledging this, the agent confirms they'll proceed with Virtual Repair over the phone. The agent then sets expectations by informing the customer about potential service disruptions, the need to access equipment, and the approximate duration of some tests. They also assure the customer of regular check-ins during the process. After a brief clarification, the customer confirms they are "Ok" to start, and the agent initiates the process.

This exchange demonstrates the system's ability to:

Proactively offer and explain a self-service troubleshooting tool.

Adapt its approach by providing a phone-guided alternative when the customer declines app usage.

Clearly set expectations and prepare the customer for the upcoming troubleshooting process.
